text.p: Osprey Maritime Ltd said on Tuesday it will acquire 100 percent of Monaco-based Gotaas-Larsen Shipping Corporation for US$750 million.
The acquisition will be from GL Holdings Corp, a Liberian company based in Monaco, Osprey said in a statement.

The purchase includes a total of nine vessels, made up of four liquefied natural gas (LNG) vessels, four very large crude carriers (VLCC) and a half-share of an LNG vessel which is already 50-percent owned by Osprey.

"The acquisition of Gotaas-Larsen is in line with the company's strategic plan, adding both to its fleet of LNG and crude carriers and broadening the group's management capability and expertise, establishing Osprey as a major international energy transportation group based in Singapore," said Timothy Cottew, chairman of Osprey.
After the acquisition, Osprey would own 30 vessels and manage another six LNG carriers making it one of Asia's largest energy transportation groups.
Its total assets would amount to US$1.36 billion and it has over US$600 million of committed future revenues.
The acquisition would be financed by net new debt of US$493 million from syndicated loan facilities and new equity of US$257 million.

The new equity comprises an issue of new shares to GL Holdings of about US$60 million, a rights issue of new shares of U$$144 million and a rights issue of redeemable cumulative convertible preference shares of US$53 million.
